data.title: The Missing Queen
data.rumour: That chess man on the Green took forty bucks off somebody's brother-in-law.
about: Gus Lindqvist, who hustles chess on the Green, borrows $20 against his 1961 boxwood set, whose white queen is a salt shaker since the real one went off the seawall (§{gusPawn}). A man from Connecticut wants a $100 game, and Gus asks you to bring the set and a proper queen from your shelves.

At the stone table (§{queenGame}) lend him a statuette, candlestick, goblet, vase or music box to stand in as queen, or let him use the salt shaker, then back Gus, bet against him, or just watch. With a real queen he wins, splits the money, and gives you the set (Checkmate); with the salt shaker he loses to a man who was no casual player (Hustled).

gusChess.name: Gus's chess set (no queen)
tells: Boxwood and ebony, older than Gus. The white queen is a salt shaker.
Someone has carved G.L. under the board, and the date 1961.

gusPawn.title: Gus wants $20 against his chess set

text: Gus Lindqvist. I play chess on the Green. For money, when the weather holds.
You may have heard I took forty dollars off a man's brother-in-law. It was forty-five. Rounding is for losers.

I need twenty dollars until the weekend. You can hold my set. Boxwood and ebony, 1961. The white queen is a salt shaker. The real one went off the seawall in a sacrifice that, I'll admit, was theatrical.

choose.label: Lend him $20 and hold the set

then.text: Your loss. Literally, if you'd played me.

steps.why: Lent Gus Lindqvist $20 against his chess set

text: One lunchtime this week, a man from Connecticut wants a game. I'll send word. A hundred dollars. I'll need the set back for an hour.
And a proper queen, if you have one. Anything that stands up straight and looks like it means it. You have shelves.

steps.toast: Calendar: Gus's game on the Green, at lunch

steps.narrate: Harbor Green at lunch. The stone table by the memorial, a pigeon, and a man in boat shoes who says he's "only a casual player" twice before he sits down.

steps.text: The set. Good. And a queen? Tell me you brought a queen.

steps.note: anything on the shelves that would stand up as a queen

choose.label: Lend him the {queens.0.name|lower} as a queen

then.text: A {queen.name|lower}. She's enormous. She's magnificent. Nobody is taking her.

choose.label: Lend him the {queens.1.name|lower} as a queen

then.text: A {queen.name|lower}. She's enormous. She's magnificent. Nobody is taking her.

choose.label: Lend him the {queens.2.name|lower} as a queen

then.text: A {queen.name|lower}. She's enormous. She's magnificent. Nobody is taking her.

choose.label: The salt shaker will have to do

then.text: Salt it is. I've won with worse. Not often.

steps.text: A hundred, then. Unless the shopkeeper wants a side bet? Twenty?

choose.label: Bet on the man in boat shoes ($20)

narrate.then: Gus plays like a man with something to protect. Every time the stranger reaches for the queen, Gus looks at him, and he doesn't.
narrate.else: It goes well until move twenty, when Gus picks up his queen and salts the board by mistake. The man in boat shoes stops being a casual player very suddenly.

then.text: Checkmate. Me. I mean you. You checkmated me. I'll go.

then.why: Gus split his winnings with you

then.text: Half the hundred, as promised. And keep the set, queen and all. I'm going out on top. The pigeon can have my table.

set.name: Gus's chess set
tells: Boxwood and ebony, 1961, with a queen that means it.

else.text: Good game. Same time next year? I'll be in Maine by then.
He was no casual player. Keep the set. I can't look at it today. I'll be back for it. Probably.

errands.title: Gus's game
errands.where: the stone table on Harbor Green

epilogue.line: Gus Lindqvist retired undefeated. He still sits at the stone table by the memorial and tells people how.
